Main findings

Look beyond one region

304/852 postings (35.7%) name at least one location outside California. New York appears in 225 and Washington in 86. Location counts overlap.

Graduate evidence needs its own filter

42/852 postings explicitly identify a graduate pathway. The 66 Entry labels also include inferred experience; they do not all establish graduate eligibility.

Learning priorities differ by direction

SQL appears in 66/79 Data Science postings (83.5%). Kubernetes appears in 66/183 ML Infrastructure postings (36.1%). These are mentions in the sample.

Counts refer to unique postings in the 2026-09-21 snapshot, not hires. State and skill counts can overlap. The sample is purposive; 795 postings are automated discovery and 57 have curated source review.

Two decisions the data can inform

  1. Broaden location comparisons. Students and career groups should compare non-California locations before narrowing their exploration. The 304 postings with a non-California location provide a concrete starting set; inspect the actual location and remote restrictions.
  2. Use separate learning tracks. Career groups can offer a SQL-focused Data Science session and a Kubernetes-focused infrastructure session, based on the 66/79 and 66/183 mention counts. Students can then use Skill lab to choose one project suited to their existing skills; mention frequency alone does not establish a course prerequisite.

Interpretation

198 postings have unspecified experience, 101 have no named US state, and 36 have no tracked skills. Skill lab scores 816 postings and uses the same fixed 70% target throughout. Missing data is not evidence of no requirements.

This sample cannot establish national demand, proficiency, eligibility or hiring probability. The methodology note explains collection, bias, definitions and the source trail. Skill selections stay in your browser.
